name: Slow Cooker Salsa Chicken Burrito Bowl
intro_html: This is a burrito bowl built for meal prep and built for a budget. A few cheap ingredients go in the slow cooker and turn into tender, saucy shredded chicken while you go about your day. Pile it over rice with black beans and cheddar, and you have two weeks of dinners that taste like takeout.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2495 g)
Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 1 can (113 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 6 lb: ~$12.27. Buy 6 lbs: $13.38.
Diced Green Chiles, 1 can: ~$1.09. Buy 1 (covers this batch).
Pantry seasonings (taco seasoning): ~$0.89. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $29.03 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.07 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $31.17 across 14 servings, roughly $2.23 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $0.13 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $31.30. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Buy dry rice, not the microwave pouches. A few cups of dry rice costs a dollar or two and stretches across all 14 bowls. The pre-cooked cups cost several times more for the same food.
Stock up on canned black beans when they go on sale. They keep for years in the pantry, so grab a few extra cans whenever they drop below a dollar.
Make your own taco seasoning if you can. Chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt do the same job as the little packets for a lot less money.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Place the chicken breast in the bottom of the slow cooker and sprinkle the taco seasoning over the top.
Add the can of diced green chiles and pour the salsa over everything so the chicken is covered.
Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 3 hours, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Shred the chicken with two forks and stir it back into the salsa so every piece soaks up the flavor.
Cook the rice, drain and warm the black beans, and add both to your empty weighed mixing pot.
Fold the salsa chicken into the rice and beans, then stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts through.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down, and divide the remaining weight by 14. That is your grams per container. Scoop each bowl to that exact weight so the servings stay honest, and you will hit roughly {{protein}} grams of protein per bowl.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from The Protein Chef, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Fourteen burrito bowls that beat the drive-thru on price, protein, and how good you feel eating them. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
